svg.title: Scene 64: The double slit: stripes made of single dots
svg.desc: Five frames. 1, a source sends particles, electrons, photons or even large molecules, towards a barrier with two slits; the screen behind shows a striped intensity pattern. 2, the particles arrive one at a time and each lands as a single dot; the stripes appear only after many dots. 3, when a detector records which slit each particle passed through, the stripes vanish and only a smooth, stripe-free spread remains. 4, the environment can carry away the same which-slit information, stray light, heat and gas molecules, so the stripes wash out: decoherence, the reason qubits are cooled and isolated. 5, a note that the stripes are in the probabilities of where whole particles land, not ripples of a substance, and that circuit interference (Scene 63) is amplitudes adding in a calculation the hardware carries out.
svg.text: The double slit: stripes made of single dots
Interference is real in nature. What it is not: tiny particles behaving as ripples.
